newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan's Adamjee Insurance 1996 profits seen up.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan's Adamjee Insurance 1996 profits seen up.

text.p: Pakistan's blue-chip Adamjee Insurance Co Ltd, buoyed by a capital gains tax exemption, is likely to show higher profits when its calendar 1996 results are announced on Wednesday, a research report said.

Waheed Hassan, an analyst at brokerage house Khalim Ali Shah Bukhari and Co Ltd, said in the report that a capital gains tax exemption granted in November would generate a tax saving of 16 million rupees ($396,000) and improve profitability.
The exemption, applicable across the sector, would enable Adamjee to realise a greater portion of its unrealised capital gains from investment portfolio, he said.
"Higher realised capital gains accompanied by tax exemption is expected to boost 1996 earnings by 47 million rupees. We expect earnings from capital gains to increase to 76 million rupees by 1999."
Earnings per 10-rupee share were likely to rise to 9.27 rupees from 7.48 in 1995, he said.
Hassan said Adamjee's ratio of retained to gross premium had increased to 63 percent in 1996 from 62.5 percent in 1995.
"The increased premium retention ratio also implies that any increase in gross premium will be translated into higher earnings growth and hence higher profitability," he said.
Earnings were likely to grow 26 percent over the next three years. "Once again Adamjee proved its leadership by achieving the 1996 gross premium target of 2.9 billion rupees," he said.
This indicated its inherent strength to absorb losses without any significant impact on earnings, he added.
Adamjee rose 1.25 rupees, or 1.11 percent, to 114.25 in early trade at the Karachi bourse on Tuesday on hopes of good corporate results and payouts after Wednesday's board meeting, dealers said.

The company has already paid a 15 percent interim cash dividend for 1996. In 1995 it made total payments of a 35 percent cash dividend and 25 percent bonus issues, which pushed its paid-up capital to 250 million rupees.
